screens.title: Which price, which weight
screens.prose:
You chose out-of-the-money quotes, read their vol bands and saw where bands widen. A fit targets each mid's vol, weighted by $w = 1/(\sigma_{\text{ask}} - \sigma_{\text{bid}})$, so loose quotes count less:

```python
otm = otm_quotes(df_T, F)
ivs = iv_from_quotes(otm, S, r, T, q)
w = 1 / (ivs["iv_ask"] - ivs["iv_bid"])
```

widget.solution:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# clean = clean_quotes(make_chain()) is loaded.

def otm_quotes(df_T, F):
    """Puts struck below F and calls struck at or above F, by strike."""
    keep = (((df_T["type"] == "put") & (df_T["strike"] < F))
            | ((df_T["type"] == "call") & (df_T["strike"] >= F)))
    return df_T[keep].sort_values("strike").reset_index(drop=True)

def iv_from_quotes(df_T, S, r, T, q):
    """Implied vols at the bid, the mid and the ask, one row per quote."""

widget.solution:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# implied_vol(price, S, K, r, T, kind, q) is loaded: NaN when no vol fits.
# mid(df) is loaded too.

def iv_from_quotes(df_T, S, r, T, q):
    """Implied vols at the bid, the mid and the ask, one row per quote."""
    rows = []
    for K, kind, b, m, a in zip(df_T["strike"], df_T["type"], df_T["bid"],
                                mid(df_T), df_T["ask"]):
        rows.append([K, kind,
                     implied_vol(b, S, K, r, T, kind, q),
                     implied_vol(m, S, K, r, T, kind, q),
                     implied_vol(a, S, K, r, T, kind, q)])
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["strike", "type", "iv_bid", "iv_mid", "iv_ask"])

screens.title: Quoting in vol
screens.prose: Over the phone a vol trader quotes the three-month 100 call in vol points: "21.5 bid, 22.5 offered". Her desk converts each vol to a price with Black-Scholes, $S = 100$, $r = 5\%$, $q = 1\%$.
screens.question: How wide is her quote in pounds per share?

widget.label: Width in pounds
widget.accept: About £0.197: one vol point times vega, about £0.197

hints.text: The width is the price at 22.5% minus the price at 21.5%.
One vol point times vega, the slope of the curve.
Read the two prices off the curve where it meets the dashed lines.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Price both vols and subtract.

byKey.points: You read one vol point as one pound. Vega converts it: about £0.20 per point here.
byKey.screen: That is the screen's price spread. Hers is set in vol, so convert it.

explain.text: One vol point is worth about £0.197 on this call, so her quote is £0.20 wide. In vol, quotes at every strike and expiry compare directly. A desk calibrates to such bands, not one number: any surface inside every band is consistent with the market.

ideas: A quote's bid and ask are a band of prices, so they are a band of vols. Calibrate to the mid where the band is tight; carry the band where it is wide.
Use out-of-the-money quotes only: puts below the forward, calls at or above it. In-the-money ones add nothing parity does not give, and can sit below the no-arbitrage bound.
Vol bands widen where vega is small: short expiries and the wings. Weight each quote by one over its band.
summary.trap: The average of the bid and ask vols is not the vol of the mid price. Price bends against vol in the wings.
